section.heading: Offences relating to dealing with examinable food

content.p: Dealing with food where no food control certificate
A person commits an offence if:
the person deals with food in a particular manner; and
the food is examinable food; and
the person knows that the food has been imported into Australia; and
the person knows that a food control certificate has not been issued in respect of the food; and
the person has not obtained the approval of an authorised officer to deal with the food in that manner; and
the person is not dealing with the food in that manner in accordance with a compliance agreement; and
the person is neither an officer of Customs, nor an authorised officer, acting in the course of his or her duties.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person deals with food in a particular manner; and
the food is examinable food; and

a food control certificate has not been issued in respect of the food; and

section.heading: Power to require information or documents

content.p: If the Secretary believes on reasonable grounds that a person has information or documents relevant to the operation of this Act, the Secretary may, by written notice, require the person:

However, the Secretary may specify a shorter period if the Secretary considers it necessary to do so because the information or documents relate to food that the Secretary is satisfied may pose a risk to human health and the Secretary is satisfied that the risk is serious.
A notice under subsection (1) must set out the effect of the following provisions:
subsection (5);
(b) section 137.1 of the Criminal Code (about giving false or misleading information);
(c) section 137.2 of the Criminal Code (about producing false or misleading documents).

the person fails to comply with the notice.

section.heading: Secretary may inspect and copy records

content.p: The Secretary may inspect a record produced under this Part and may make and retain copies of the whole or a part of the record.
The Secretary may take, and retain for as long as is reasonably necessary, possession of a record produced under this Part.
The person otherwise entitled to possession of the record is entitled to be supplied, as soon as practicable, with a copy certified by the Secretary to be a true copy.
The certified copy must be received in all courts and tribunals as evidence as if it were the original.

Until a certified copy is supplied, the Secretary must, at such times and places as the Secretary thinks appropriate, permit the person otherwise entitled to possession of the record, or a person authorised by that person, to inspect and make copies of the record.
A person is not excused from producing a record under this Part on the ground that the production of the record might tend to incriminate the person or expose the person to a penalty.
However, in the case of an individual:
the record; and
producing the record; and
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of producing the record;
are not admissible in evidence against the individual in criminal proceedings other than:
proceedings for an offence against subsection 28(4) or 29(5); or
(e) proceedings for an offence against section 137.1 or 137.2 of the Criminal Code that relates to this Part.
